# dmr-radio (device class)

> DMR handhelds being programmed over USB — codeplug read and write

DMR handhelds — Anytone, TYT, Baofeng, Radioddity and their rebadges — seen from the Linux side while being programmed. Most of the time that is an ordinary USB serial connection; for some radios it is a bare microcontroller in a bootloader.

## Devices in this class

*None catalogued yet.*

## Shared setup

Install `qdmr` or `dmrconfig`, join `dialout`, then log out and back in — group membership does not apply to a session already open. Attach the radio with its programming cable and read the codeplug BEFORE writing one, so there is something to go back to.

## Shared tooling

[`dfu-util`](../packages/dfu-util.md), [`dmrconfig`](../packages/dmrconfig.md), [`qdmr`](../packages/qdmr.md)
